poc_iosize.settings_rules: read sizes: power of two, >= block size, <= 8mb; default = block size (one block per miss). Invalid values stop the node at startup. All three are static node settings (restart to change).
poc_iosize.random_vs_sequential: decided per input like mmapfs/hybridfs (MMapDirectory.ADVISE_BY_CONTEXT): MERGE/FLUSH -> sequential; DataAccessHint.RANDOM -> random; DataAccessHint.SEQUENTIAL -> sequential; else Lucene default read advice (NORMAL unless -Dorg.apache.lucene.store.defaultReadAdvice) -> sequential. In this Lucene, only stored fields (.fdt), term vectors and vector data open with RANDOM; doc values, BKD, postings and terms read 128 KiB per miss. Compound-file sub-files keep their own context (slice with IOContext).
poc_iosize.prefetch: prefetch ranges are aligned to and coalesced into 128 KiB windows; a window is read only if a requested block in it is missing; each prefetch call still reads its windows one after another on one prefetch thread (same in-flight depth as before)
poc_iosize.planner_node_bytes: all prefetch planners get node size = bufferpool.io.sequential_read_size at node start and on every experiment POST (DocValuesPrefetch, TopKPrefetch, BKDExperiments (min 4 KiB), SortIoExperiments; DisjunctionPrefetch when aligned). The 'blocks' parameters of /_bufferpool/disjunction_prefetch and /_bufferpool/topk_prefetch now count nodes of this size.
poc_iosize.new_stats: GET /_bufferpool/stats: random_read_size, sequential_read_size, prefetch_node_bytes, in_flight_reads; per file type: reads, prefetch_reads, bytes_read, reads_by_size{class upper bound bytes: count}, readahead_loads, blocks_inserted (loads + prefetch_loads + readahead_loads), bytes_loaded (inserted bytes). Trace events have 'readahead'; readahead_unread is reported apart from prefetched_unread.
poc_iosize.harness_note: the cold harness's first-read-is-a-miss check (loads + prefetch_loads) still works; IO-size verification should read bytes_read and reads_by_size, and the NFS client counters (nfsiostat) for the bytes requested from EFS per read

poc_iosize2.what: Interim POC binary = artifacts 'poc' (poc-ioopt 24d19cc03e9 + Lucene bkd-split 59f87aa1af) plus the bufferpool storage layer after the bp-iosize review fixes (ec2-bench eb26156111a on 3aa118fac02): one storage read per whole IO window, read hints (posix_fadvise WILLNEED per window, so a window is one device IO with read_ahead_kb=0), window/overread/wait/prefetch-queue counters, and the prefetch task-per-window switch (off by default). Use it for every S1/S2 arm and for the storage-layer attribution arms SL-0/SL-H/SL-W/SL-WN (experiments/EXP-SL1-bp-iosize/hypothesis.md Amendment 1).
poc_iosize2.os_commit_subject: Make each bufferpool IO window one storage read

poc_iosize2.settings_rules: read sizes: power of two, >= block size, <= 8mb; default = block size. read_hint: auto|willneed|none; willneed refuses to start where posix_fadvise is unavailable. Static except task_per_window (dynamic, PUT _cluster/settings). Invalid values stop the node at startup.
poc_iosize2.window_reads: every demand miss and prefetch reads its whole aligned window with ONE pread (EOF-clipped): 32 KiB for DataAccessHint.RANDOM inputs (decided like mmapfs ADVISE_BY_CONTEXT), 128 KiB otherwise. Blocks of the window that are cached or being read by another thread are not replaced or waited for; their bytes are dropped (bytes_overread).
poc_iosize2.read_hints: each window pread is preceded by posix_fadvise(WILLNEED) of exactly the window on a second read-only fd of the file (JNA, reference counted). With read_ahead_kb=0 that makes the window one device IO (without it Linux reads 4 KiB pages one by one). Each open file of a bufferpool index holds two fds.
poc_iosize2.prefetch: prefetch ranges aligned to and coalesced into 128 KiB windows; a window is read only if a requested block in it is missing; one task per request (default) or one task per window (task_per_window=true).
poc_iosize2.planner_node_bytes: unchanged from poc_iosize: every planner node size = bufferpool.io.sequential_read_size (bp-iosize-node-sizes.md).
poc_iosize2.new_stats: GET /_bufferpool/stats adds node-wide read_hint, read_hints, read_hint_errors, prefetch_task_per_window, pending_prefetch_tasks, rejected_prefetch_tasks, multi_window_prefetches, max_prefetch_reads_in_flight; per file type bytes_overread, window_blocks, window_blocks_cached, window_blocks_in_flight, waits, wait_time_micros. Identities per file type: bytes_read == bytes_loaded + bytes_overread; window_blocks == blocks_inserted + window_blocks_cached + window_blocks_in_flight. Quiet cache = in_flight_reads == 0 and pending_prefetch_tasks == 0.
poc_iosize2.harness_note: the cold harness's first-read-is-a-miss check (loads + prefetch_loads) still works. The one-device-read-per-window check holds for SL-H, SL-W and every S1/S2 arm (read_hint willneed); it must expect 2 device IOs per 8 KiB read on SL-0 and 32 / 8 per 128 / 32 KiB read on SL-WN (read_hint none), which are those arms' mechanism.

poc_iosize_conc.what: poc_iosize3 storage layer and the approved codec commits of ec2-bench (up to 3760a9eb88d and the storage branch 63a89302765) plus node-wide prefetch concurrency (bp-concurrency-design.md revision 9 with addendum 14): settings bufferpool.prefetch.max_in_flight (1-256, default min(8, processors)), budget_scope (prefetch default | total), queue_size (0-65536, default 1024), queue_policy (fifo default | fair); PrefetchScheduler (bounded queue, drop never defer, budget gate over prefetch or prefetch+demand reads in flight, demand reads counted never throttled), PrefetchTaskListener (cancellation and query fairness key), /_bufferpool/stats prefetch_scheduler object and latency histograms (?histogram_buckets=true). With no new settings the node behaves as poc_iosize3 except: a cancelled search's queued prefetches are dropped, and the bufferpool_prefetch thread-pool queue is 8 worker runnables (items queue in the scheduler; read prefetch_scheduler.items_started / pending instead of thread-pool completed / queue). Rebuilt at 807d8509e56 with the fixes of code review iteration 1 (bp-concurrency-code-review.md): the stats readers (GET /_bufferpool/stats, its reset) run the kick loop after they unlock, so a held item is never left without a wake-up; a submit that finds the gate reopened while items wait gives the slot to the next queued item by the policy; items_started and items_started_after_phase_end count items a worker ran (a cancelled item is in dropped.cancelled only); the histograms record nanoseconds and report microseconds with a fraction.
